# [TASK] Professional Kibana dashboard suite (Lens, multi-dashboard, alerting)

## Task
Rebuild the local ELK stack's Kibana experience into a real, portfolio-quality observability suite, built with the modern Lens editor — not just the one existing legacy-Visualize-editor dashboard (`filmpire-overview.ndjson`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] 3 Kibana Lens dashboards: Service Health (log volume/level trends per service), Error Triage (errors over time, top error loggers, recent-errors table), Per-Service Deep-Dive (log stream + level trend, filterable by service)
- [x] Interactive Controls dropdown filtering by `application`
- [x] `filmpire-logs-*` data view has field formatting on `level` (red ERROR, orange WARN)
- [x] 1-2 Alerting rules (e.g. ERROR-rate threshold per service) using a no-external-creds connector (server log or index)
- [x] All saved objects checked into `infrastructure/docker/elk/kibana/*.ndjson`, imported by `setup.sh` on every `docker-compose up`

## Not in scope
- APM / request-latency dashboards (no distributed tracing yet, that's #42)
- ML anomaly detection (Elasticsearch Basic license locally, no ML)
- A Kibana homepage linking the 3 dashboards — filed as its own follow-up now that the 3 dashboards exist

## Verification
Built and verified against a live ELK stack (this session had a Docker/podman daemon, unlike the prior autonomous-sandbox attempts):
- All 3 dashboards, the Controls dropdown, and the alerting rules were checked visually with Playwright screenshots against the running Kibana, against real accumulated log data (~2M docs across 7 services).
- The `level` color formatting was confirmed in Discover (WARN cells render with the orange background, independent of any text-highlight).
- Both alerting rules use the built-in `.server-log` connector (no external creds); one rule actually fired end-to-end against real WARN/ERROR volume and logged to the Kibana server log.
- Wired into `infrastructure/docker/elk/setup/setup.sh` via two new files, `filmpire-lens-suite.ndjson` and `filmpire-alerting.ndjson`, imported after the existing `filmpire-overview.ndjson` (order matters: Error Triage's "Recent Errors" panel references a saved search owned by that first file). Re-ran the whole `elk-setup` container against the already-running stack (the same path a real `docker-compose up` takes) and confirmed the field formatting, all 3 dashboards, and both rules (enabled) came back correctly.
- Kibana needed `xpack.encryptedSavedObjects.encryptionKey` set for alerting/connectors to work at all (500s otherwise) — added to `docker-compose.elk.yml` and `.env.example` as `KIBANA_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, defaulted for local dev since this profile already runs with `xpack.security` disabled.

## Estimate
**Hours:** not estimated (closed before hour estimates were required)

## Notes
Prior sessions in the autonomous sandbox correctly identified this as blocked (no Docker daemon there). Done here in a Docker-capable session — the Lens/dashboard saved-object JSON was built by scripting Kibana's REST API directly rather than hand-authoring it, then verified live rather than assumed correct.
